title: Data Synchronization Strategies
description: Learn strategies for synchronizing data between microservices with database per service.

data.text: When each service owns its data, you need strategies to keep related data synchronized. Amazon, Netflix, and LinkedIn use change data capture, event-based synchronization, and background reconciliation jobs to maintain data consistency across services.

data.title: Data Synchronization Approaches
items: Application events: Service publishes events when data changes
Change data capture (CDC): Stream database changes using tools like Debezium
Polling: Periodically query for changes (simple but inefficient)
Background jobs: Reconcile differences between services periodically
API calls: Explicitly call other services when data changes

data.text: CDC captures row-level changes in the database and streams them to other services. This decouples services and ensures that data changes are propagated reliably. Debezium, AWS DMS, and SQL Server CDC are popular implementations.

data.title: Debezium
data.text: Debezium is an open-source CDC platform that connects to databases like PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB, and streams change events to Kafka. Netflix and LinkedIn use Debezium for data synchronization.

data.caption: CDC data synchronization flow
data.definition:
graph LR
    DB[(User DB)] -->|CDC Stream| D[Debezium]
    D -->|Change Events| K[Kafka]
    K -->|Consume| S1[Search Service]
    K -->|Consume| S2[Analytics Service]
    K -->|Consume| S3[Notification Service]
    S1 -->|Update| ES[(Elasticsearch)]
    S2 -->|Update| DW[(Data Warehouse)]
    S3 -->|Send| E[Email]

items.question: What is the difference between CDC and application events?
items.answer: CDC captures changes at the database level without modifying application code. Application events are published by the service code. CDC is more reliable but harder to debug.

items.question: How do I handle schema changes with CDC?
items.answer: CDC tools like Debezium handle schema evolution by including schema information in the change events. Consumers must be able to handle schema changes gracefully.

items.question: What about data conflicts?
items.answer: Use idempotent consumers and version vectors to handle conflicts. CDC ensures at-least-once delivery, so consumers must be idempotent.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CDC captures database changes without application changes
Events enable loose coupling between services
Background jobs reconcile differences as a safety net
Choose the strategy that fits your consistency requirements
data.takeaway: Data synchronization is essential for database per service; combine multiple strategies for robustness.
